risk_reasons: **Critical path logic**: The spec modifies the fix-loop resolution logic in build-implement.js that determines whether disputed findings pass verification. The five new decision functions (disputesToJudge, resolveRound, roundOutcome, testRepairTarget, unlandedRepairs) are injected into the core loop that gates whether changes integrate, making errors in these functions block or incorrectly permit changes.

**Venture 0 self-modification**: This repository is the product (venture 0), and the change modifies the build line's own verifier panel. A mistake in the verification gate logic affects the entire product's ability to validate future builds.

**System-wide impact, not isolated route**: Per the prompt, this is NOT low-risk because a mistake in the resolution logic weakens EVERY future build (not just one route). A single bug in roundOutcome, disputesToJudge, or resolveRound cascades across all future work items, potentially allowing unresolved HIGH-severity findings to integrate repeatedly.

**Verification gate control**: The spec adds the roundOutcome guard that is the sole route to `passed: true`. If this guard is incorrectly implemented, the verification system can return false positives (pass when findings remain unresolved) or false negatives (escalate when findings are actually resolved), breaking the integrity of the build pipeline.

**Audit and provenance impact**: The changes feed directly into the Method Ledger (via Escalation.reasons and resolution states). A mistake in how findings are marked 'resolved'/'unresolved'/'upheld'/'overruled' corrupts the provenance record and the measurement basis for the entire graph system.

**Testability constraint limits verification**: The constraint that this fix cannot execute itself (only the committed copy runs) and is verifiable only via unit tests in substrate/test/, not live observation, means mistakes may not surface until real builds execute the changed logic against production disputes.

design.disputesToJudge: selects disputes for the judge WITHOUT looking at which repair path produced them — closes the kind===code filter that is the defect
design.resolveRound: sets resolution for EVERY dedupe_key given (raised, carried-in, deferred, repaired); nobody-resolved becomes unresolved and is CARRIED
design.roundOutcome: a green panel is green only when nothing is carried — this is the guard that makes k1v impossible
design.testRepairTarget: points the test repair at the file the finding cites, not at the .artifacts copy
design.unlandedRepairs: a skipped basename the repair path edited forces the strong-model integrate:resolve pass instead of being dropped

payload.a6_handling: task owns ONLY .claude/workflows/build-implement.js; the TestSet is the Test Author artifact and lands at integration. AC-17 is explicitly labelled CHANGE-SCOPED and panel-verified.
payload.known_risk_on_this_run: AC-17 is change-scoped but still appears in the task criteria_ids. Its GIVEN says so in prose, and prose guidance is measured insufficient in this repo (A1). If the correctness lens demands a test for it, that is the k2i failure mode recurring. B3 fixes this in code; it is not fixed yet.
payload.bootstrap: build-implement runs its COMMITTED copy, so this fix cannot engage in the run that builds it. Verifiable by unit tests via the extract-fixloop sentinel idiom only.
